_what: The ONLY declared departures from byte-wise filename order in the canonical chain. scripts/src/apply-migrations.ts (orderMigrations / applyOrderOverrides) is the authority; artifacts/api-server/scripts/local-db/resolve-order.mjs implements the same algorithm for up.sh, and scripts/src/migration-order-overrides.test.ts holds the two equal on this tree. docs/migrations.md § "Apply-order overrides" is the prose.
_algorithm: Sort every *.sql filename byte-wise. Then apply the entries below IN LIST ORDER. A MOVE ({move, before|after}) removes `move` and re-inserts it immediately before `before` (or immediately after `after`). A SKIP ({skip, superseded_by}) removes `skip` from the chain: it is never applied, never pending, and the harness never runs it; a real apply records it, if it has no ledger row, with applied_by='backfill' and checksum='backfill' (2254's semantics: the filename exists, nothing ran), ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. Nothing else moves. An entry naming a file that is not on disk (moved, skipped, anchor or superseded_by) is a HARD REFUSAL (the applier exits 2, the harness aborts) — a stale override is never silently ignored. This file is not a migration: every reader of src/migrations filters on .sql.
_rule: An entry exists only for a MEASURED fact about what the reference database (portava-ci) actually received or holds, with its ledger provenance in `evidence`. Never add one to paper over a new migration's ordering: a NEW migration must sort correctly by its own number.

overrides.why: 2136 has two preconditions satisfied only by files that sort after it. Its second DO block refuses while any FK to public.profiles is NO ACTION/RESTRICT, or SET NULL onto a NOT NULL column — 2138_profiles_fk_convergence_prep.sql performs those 61 conversions (its header: "Prerequisite for 2136"). Its third DO block refuses while any of 16 shared-content tables keeps a CASCADE edge to profiles — 2139_shared_content_tombstones.sql re-rules them (its header: "Second prerequisite for 2136, whose third precondition refuses until this lands"). Placing 2136 after 2139 puts both before it. In byte order a clean replay refuses "PRECONDITION FAILED: 54 foreign key(s) to public.profiles would reject a cascading delete"; with only 2138 moved ahead of it, it refuses "PRECONDITION FAILED: 14 CASCADE edge(s) would DELETE records belonging to other users".
overrides.evidence: portava-ci: PR #111 (claude/d6-rulings-20260823, merged 2026-08-23) introduced 2138 and 2139 as 2136's prerequisites and applied 2138 before 2136; the ledger rows for 2136 and 2138 are applied_by='backfill' (pre-ledger, 2254's seed), so the ledger cannot order them and 2136's own preconditions do. Replay, CI's postgis/postgis:16-3.4 (ci.yml api-server-local-db): byte order — run 37442240254 (main b102255da) refuses 2136 in order and applies it on the post-chain retry, i.e. once 2138 AND 2139 have run; 2138-before-2136 only — run 37445105786 refuses 2136 at the third precondition (14 edges); 2136-after-2139 — run 37446087758 replays 2136 in order.

overrides.why: 2137 drops 2130's three statement-level triggers AND public.intel_append_only_stmt() in one transaction. 2276 and 2277 require the function at their preconditions, and 2276, 2277 and 2279 each attach a statement trigger executing it; 2292 removes those and drops the function, refusing while any trigger still executes it. The state the reference database holds therefore needs 2130's triggers gone BEFORE 2292 while the function survives UNTIL 2292, and no position of 2137 gives that: before 2276, 2276 refuses "2130 append-only trigger functions are missing" (2277, 2278, 2279, 2292, 3002, 3003, 3310 follow); between 2276 and 2292, "cannot drop function intel_append_only_stmt() because other objects depend on it"; after 2292, 2292's postcondition refuses because 2130's three triggers still execute the function. 2134 re-issues 2137's trigger half without the function drop, and 2292 is the file that drops the function, so 2137 itself is never applied.
overrides.evidence: portava-ci ledger: 2137 applied_by='backfill' (unverified, 2254's seed); 2276 applied_by='ci' 2026-09-04 15:27:27, whose precondition required the function; 2292 applied_by='manual' 2026-09-05 11:36:06. portava-ci state read 2026-10-06: intel_append_only_stmt() absent, intel_append_only() present, no *_no_update_delete_stmt trigger on any intel table, the *_no_truncate guards present. Replay, CI's postgis/postgis:16-3.4: byte order — run 37442240254 (2276 and seven after it fail); 2137 after 2279 — run 37445105786 ("cannot drop function intel_append_only_stmt() because other objects depend on it").

overrides.why: 2140's postcondition requires user_deletion_requests' status CHECK to permit 'completed'. The replay's baseline is PRODUCTION's 2026-08-19 structure, whose CHECK is status IN ('pending','cancelled','executed'); 2178 is the file that adds 'completed'. In byte order (and with 2136 replaying ahead of it) 2140 refuses "POSTCONDITION FAILED: status CHECK does not permit 'completed', which AccountDeletionService writes;". This entry reproduces the CHECK 2140 found on portava-ci, not the calendar order: 2140 (committed 2026-08-23) predates 2178 (2026-08-27) and passed there because portava-ci's CHECK always had 'completed'.
overrides.evidence: Baseline: baseline/20260819_baseline_structure.sql, user_deletion_requests_status_check = ('pending','cancelled','executed'). portava-ci status CHECK read 2026-10-06: status = ANY (ARRAY['pending','executing','cancelled','executed','completed','failed']); 2178's header records that CI always had 'completed'. No file in 2141-2177 references user_deletion_requests. Replay, CI's postgis/postgis:16-3.4: run 37446087758 refuses 2140 in order with 2136 already replayed; the post-chain retry (after 2178) applies it in runs 37442240254 and 37446482143.
